chunks.title: H-1B Cap Season — The H-1B Program
chunks.text: The H-1B program allows companies and other employers in the United States to temporarily employ foreign workers in occupations that require the theoretical and practical application of a body of highly specialized knowledge and a bachelor’s degree or higher in a directly related specific specialty (or its equivalent) as a minimum for entry into the occupation in the United States.

chunks.title: H-1B Cap Season — The H-1B Cap
chunks.text: Congress set the current annual regular cap for the H-1B category at 65,000 (commonly known as the “regular cap”). An additional 20,000 petitions filed on behalf of beneficiaries who have earned a master’s degree or higher from a U.S. institution of higher education are exempt from the cap. Not all H-1B nonimmigrant visas (or status grants) are subject to this annual cap (for example, petitions filed by U.S. institutions of higher education are cap exempt).

chunks.title: H-1B Specialty Occupations — Electronic Registration Process
chunks.text: In 2020, we implemented an electronic registration process for the H-1B cap. We will not consider a cap-subject H-1B petition to be properly filed unless it is based on a valid, selected registration for the same beneficiary and the appropriate fiscal year, unless the registration requirement is suspended.

chunks.title: H-1B Specialty Occupations — Labor Condition Application
chunks.text: Prospective specialty occupation and distinguished fashion model employers or agents must obtain a certification of an LCA from the DOL. The prospective petitioner must include evidence that a Form ETA-9035/9035E, Labor Condition Application (LCA) has been certified by the Department of Labor (DOL), with Form I-129, Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker.
